title: Revised Julian Calendar
intro: The Revised Julian calendar refines the original Julian leap cycle to reduce long-term seasonal drift.
structure: A year not divisible by four is common. A non-century year divisible by four is leap. A century year is leap only if its remainder modulo 900 is 200 or 600.
model: The provider implements Milankovic's 1923 leap rule arithmetically with its day-coordinate anchor at 1 January 2000, when it coincides with the Gregorian calendar. There are 218 leap years in 900 years.
example: 2000 and 2400 are leap years under both calendars. Revised Julian 2800 is common, whereas Gregorian 2800 is leap; their dates diverge after the leap-day boundary.
history: The Revised Julian rule was proposed in 1923 for Orthodox calendar reform. Churches and communities differ in adoption and use.
limits: Dates before adoption are mathematical back-projections. Ecclesiastical observance and Paschal (Easter) calculations can employ separate rules.
